guarantees.claim: msg_fifo_rdata is always driven to all-ones (32'hFFFF_FFFF).
msg_fifo_rerror is always driven to all-ones, indicating a read error.
msg_fifo_gnt is asserted (high) when msg_fifo_req is high, hmac_fifo_wsel is low, and packer_ready is high.
reg_fifo_wentry.data is the result of conv_endian32(reg_fifo_wdata, 1'b1), always performing a big-endian byte swap.
reg_fifo_wentry.mask is formed by concatenating bits 0, 8, 16, and 24 of reg_fifo_wmask, ignoring all other bits.
fifo_empty is the logical negation of fifo_rvalid.
fifo_wvalid is hmac_fifo_wvalid when hmac_fifo_wsel is high and fifo_wready is high; otherwise it is reg_fifo_wvalid.
intr_fifo_empty_o is driven by prim_intr_hw instance configured with Width=1 and IntrT="Status", using status_fifo_empty as event and connected reg2hw/hw2reg signals.
intr_hmac_err_o is driven by prim_intr_hw instance with Width=1 (default IntrT), using err_valid as event and connected reg2hw/hw2reg signals.

assumptions.claim: The event inputs status_fifo_empty and err_valid must be single-cycle, glitch‑free pulses as expected by prim_intr_hw.
assumptions.risk: Missed, extra, or metastable interrupt state.

assumptions.claim: reg_fifo_wmask bits 7:1, 15:9, 23:17, and 31:25 must be zero; only bits 0, 8, 16, 24 are used as byte enables.
assumptions.cond: when a write to the message FIFO occurs
assumptions.risk: Incorrect write data masking: intended byte lanes may not be written, or partial writes may be missed.

assumptions.claim: packer_ready must eventually be asserted when msg_fifo_req is active; otherwise the read grant will be deasserted indefinitely.
assumptions.risk: Read stall / deadlock if the external consumer cannot backpressure.

assumptions.claim: hmac_fifo_wsel must be low when a read request (msg_fifo_req) is active, because grant logic blocks reads while write select is asserted.
assumptions.cond: concurrent read/write from the message FIFO interface
assumptions.risk: Read request is never granted, causing a hang or data access failure.

uncertain_points.claim: msg_fifo_rdata and msg_fifo_rerror are forced to all-ones, effectively returning an error on any read. The intent may be to permanently disable readback of message data (potentially to protect secret key/plaintext). If so, the presence of msg_fifo_req/gnt suggests an incomplete or stubbed read interface.
uncertain_points.risk: If reads are ever expected, this is a functional bug. If it is a security hardening, the design may need explicit documentation or an additional access control mechanism.

uncertain_points.claim: reg_fifo_wmask bits other than 0,8,16,24 are silently ignored; no error is reported if they are set. The XOR reduction only serves to suppress lint warnings.
uncertain_points.cond: when software writes non-zero to upper bits of a byte lane in reg_fifo_wmask
uncertain_points.risk: Silent data corruption: writes may fail to occur in intended lanes without any alert. An error flag would allow detection of mis‑programming.
